bodyMarkdown:
## The idea in plain language

Volume is how much water a container holds. Surface area is how much wrapping paper you would need to cover it. A closed box needs paper on all six faces; an open tank needs only five.

Reading whether the shape is open or closed, solid or hollow, decides which formula applies — and that is where most marks are lost.

## What is actually going on

For any prism or cylinder, volume is simply **base area times height**. A cylinder is a circle extruded upward, so its volume is $\pi r^2 h$.

Cones and pyramids taper to a point and hold exactly **one third** as much as the prism or cylinder with the same base and height.

For surface area, decide what surfaces actually exist. A cylindrical pipe open at both ends has only the curved surface $2\pi r h$; a sealed tin adds two circular ends.

workedExamples.stemMarkdown: Find the volume of a cylinder of radius 7 cm and height 10 cm. Use $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$.
A cube of side 6 cm is melted and recast into smaller cubes of side 2 cm. How many small cubes are formed?
workedExamples.solutionMarkdown:
Volume is conserved when melting and recasting.

Large cube: $6^3 = 216$ cubic cm.
Small cube: $2^3 = 8$ cubic cm.

Number $= \dfrac{216}{8} = 27$.
workedExamples.altSolutionMarkdown: Since $6 = 3 \times 2$, the big cube is 3 small cubes along each edge: $3^3 = 27$.

formulaCards.title: Volumes
formulaCards.bodyMarkdown: Cuboid $lbh$. Cube $a^3$. Cylinder $\pi r^2 h$. Cone $\dfrac13\pi r^2 h$. Sphere $\dfrac43\pi r^3$.
formulaCards.exampleMarkdown: A cone of radius 3 and height 7 holds $\frac13 \pi \times 9 \times 7 = 21\pi$.

formulaCards.title: Surface areas
formulaCards.bodyMarkdown: Cube $6a^2$. Cylinder: curved $2\pi rh$, total $2\pi r(r+h)$. Sphere $4\pi r^2$.
formulaCards.exampleMarkdown: A closed cylinder with $r = 7$, $h = 10$ has total surface $2 \times \frac{22}{7} \times 7 \times 17 = 748$.

formulaCards.title: Melting and recasting
formulaCards.bodyMarkdown: Volume is conserved. Set the old volume equal to the new one and solve.
formulaCards.exampleMarkdown: A sphere of radius 3 recast into spheres of radius 1 gives 27 of them.

commonTraps: Including the ends of an open cylinder, or omitting them from a closed one.
Dropping the one-third for cones and pyramids.
Using slant height where vertical height is needed in a cone's volume. Volume uses the vertical height; curved surface area uses the slant.
